lectures.title: Collision Resolution Techniques - Direct Chaining Implementation

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to talk about collision resolution techniques.
Now before continuing to the technique let's see what is collision and why do we need these resolution
techniques.
So here we have a hash function and we have hash table.
Let's say we want to insert this key value pair to this hash table.
So in this case as we mentioned before we are taking the key which is Mongo and passing it to hashing
function.
And it's going to return the index.
And based on this index we are going to insert this key value pair to this hash table.
So it's returned three.
And we have inserted it at the index of three.
Now if I continue to insert one more key value pair over here, let's say in this case we want to insert
Apple with the value of 11.
So here again we are going to take Apple and pass it over here to this function.
And it's going to return the index.
So let's say it's also returning index of three.
Now at the index of three we have another key value pair.
So if we try to insert this to the same index, it's going to cause collision.
Now the question is how can we solve this problem.
Now for this we have collision resolution techniques.
Now there are two types of collision resolution techniques.
So here the first type is direct chaining which is called separate chaining also.
And the second one is open addressing.
Now in case of direct chaining we are going to implement a reimplementation and linked list implementation.
And we are going to look at the three types of open addressing linear, quadratic and double hashing.
Now first we are going to continue with the direct chaining.
As a first implementation we are going to use array.
So let's say we have hash table like this.
And we have already inserted some key value pairs over here.
Now take into account that in case of array implementation, when we are inserting the key value pair
to this hash table over here, each value pair will be inside the array.
So in this case the key is going to be the first element in the array.
And the value is going to be the second element, which means that key is located at index of zero and
the value is located at the index of one.
Now this one also itself is an array.
So here we have the nested arrays.
Now if we want to insert for example another key value pair which is with the value of 15.

So we will have array and each key and value pair will be inserted as a elements of this array over
here.
So as you can see at this index we have nested array.
So that's how the array implementation looks like.
